newsitem.title: CANADA: Toronto stocks end lower on weaker banks.
newsitem.headline: Toronto stocks end lower on weaker banks.

text.p: Toronto stocks ended softer on Wednesday after a busy session in which investors took profits in the influential bank and conglomerate sectors.

The Toronto Stock Exchange's key 300 Composite Index slipped 13.53 points to close at 6459.51, retreating from a recent lifetime high of 6507 points set on June 9. Trading was heavy at 99.1 million shares worth C$1.6 billion ($1.1 billion).
"We've got a major search for leadership in Canadian markets," said Jim Mountain, ScotiaMcLeod's managing director of private client equity trading.
Eight of Toronto's 14 sub-indexes shed points, including conglomerates, banks, consumer products and transportation.
The stronger side was led by media and base metals.
Declining stocks beat out advancers 514 to 445, while 324 closed even.
The debut of Boliden Ltd. added interest. Boliden is a partial float of shares from Swedish mining and rubber company Trelleborg AB's Boliden unit.
Boliden closed at 8.05 on turnover of 9 million shares.
Car parts maker Magna International Inc. rose 3.10 to 76.20 after announcing that third-quarter earnings for the period ended April 30 rose to C$1.60 a share from year earlier C$1.33.

Inco Ltd. shares rose 1.10 to 30.75 on half a million shares. The nickel giant said on Wednesday that it was selling its alloys unit to Blackstone's Haynes International Inc. alloys affiliate for $410 million.
Inco said it expected to realize an after-tax gain of $85 million on the sale.
